items.text: How to report scams and cybercrime

title: How to report scams and cybercrime
introduction: This page tells you what to do if you have been scammed.

blocks.title: What scams and cybercrime are

paragraphs.text: A scam is when someone tries to trick you.
They might try to take your money.
A cybercrime is when someone uses a computer or the internet to break the law.

blocks.imgAlt: A man at a computer beside a warning message

blocks.title: Stop contacting the scammer

paragraphs.text: A scammer is a person who does a scam.
Stop calling or messaging the scammer.
Do not send them more money.

blocks.imgAlt: A woman on the phone beside a crossed-out phone

blocks.title: Contact your bank

paragraphs.text: Contact your bank if the scammer has your bank details.
Your bank can help protect your account and cards.

blocks.imgAlt: A woman calling her bank beside a bank card

blocks.title: Change your passwords

paragraphs.text: Change the passwords for your devices.
Change the passwords for your online accounts.
Use a different password for each account.

blocks.imgAlt: A man changing a password on a computer beside a lock

blocks.title: Write down the scam details

paragraphs.text: Write down information about the scammer.
This might include their phone number, email address or website.
This information can help stop the scammer.

blocks.imgAlt: A woman on the phone beside a checklist

blocks.title: Report the scam

paragraphs.text: Report the scam as soon as you can.
Call NSW Fair Trading on 13 32 20 if the scam started in NSW.
You can also report the scam to NSW Fair Trading online.
For scams outside NSW, report the scam to Scamwatch.

blocks.imgAlt: A woman reporting a scam by phone beside a completed report

blocks.title: Report cybercrime online

paragraphs.text: Use ReportCyber to report a cybercrime.
ReportCyber will send your report to the right organisation.

blocks.linkText: Report a cybercrime on the ReportCyber website
blocks.imgAlt: A man reporting cybercrime on a computer beside a safety shield

blocks.title: Get support

paragraphs.text: Tell someone you trust what happened.
Your family, friends or support person might be able to help.
Contact ID Support NSW if someone has stolen your identity.
Your identity is the information that proves who you are.

blocks.linkText: Get help from ID Support NSW
blocks.imgAlt: People getting support at a service desk beside a support symbol
